newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NSW state approves BHP gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NSW state approves BHP gas pipeline.

text.p: The New South Wales (NSW) state government said on Wednesday it had approved the permit for a 740 km underground gas pipeline from Bass Strait to Sydney.

Joint venturers, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd unit BHP Petroleum and Vancouver-based Westcoast Energy Inc unit Westcoast Energy Australia, would start work to survey the route and supply an environmental management plan, it said.
A commission of inquiry granted environmental approval for the A$380 million pipeline in September.

NSW Energy Minister Michael Egan said in a statement the pipeline would improve the environment by replacing coal in power stations and industrial heating, and bring lower gas costs through greater competition.
BHP is the partner in the Bass Strait oil and gas fields with Exxon Corp.
The pipeline is one of two proposed gas links between NSW and Victoria, with East Australian Pipeline Ltd (EAPL) and Gas Transmission Corp (GTC) planning a 146 km pipeline.
That link would allow gas from the Santos Ltd -led Cooper Basin venture in South Australia, which is now delivered to NSW via the Moomba to Sydney pipeline, to be sent to Victoria.
EAPL is 50 percent owned by NSW gas distributor Australian Gas Light Co and 50 percent by foreign investors, while GTC is owned by the state of Victoria.
